title: Hark! What Celestial Notes
description: Hark! What Celestial Notes in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 207 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the Salisbury Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.4.4.4.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! what ce-les-tial notes, What mel-o-dy, we hear! Soft on the morn it floats, And fills the rav-ished ear. The tune-ful shell, The gol-den lyre, And vo-cal choir, The con-cert swell.

lines: Soft on the morn it floats,
See, how from heaven they bend,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
